This file documents the cuts resource at the shell, one section per command. Every command is a subcommand of =cuts=, and every section exports its own script into =projects/ores.shell/scripts/library/=. Loading a script runs that one command, so a failure names the command it came from.

* Commands

** =list=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 4A409D84-090D-5D3B-A870-59356259CA9D
:END:

Reads one page of the collection. Nothing addresses it but the caller's tenant, so it is the read that shows what exists.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
cuts list [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--order <field>] [--desc]
#+end_example

It is addressed at =reporting.v1.cuts.list=.

#+name: cuts-list
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle cuts-list.ores :exports none
cuts list --limit 1
#+end_src

** =get=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 6E930DCE-8D2A-5B10-9221-A15386DDE349
:END:

Reads the one row its key addresses. A key states every identifying column, so a partial key is refused rather than answered with an arbitrary row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
cuts get <id>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =reporting.v1.cuts.get=.

#+name: cuts-get
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle cuts-get.ores :exports none
cuts get 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
#+end_src

** =by-kind-code=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 2B8D8FBB-0E92-5EFC-91F6-D58EC3FF4C7A

Reads one page of the rows that share a relation value. The relation is part of the address rather than a filter applied after the read.


The command is shaped like this:

#+end_example

It is addressed at =reporting.v1.cuts.list_by_kind_code=.

#+name: cuts-by-kind-code
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle cuts-by-kind-code.ores :exports none
cuts by-kind-code __none__ --limit 1
#+end_src
